# Sacca Saṁyutta (SN 56)

**ID:** SN 56
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Sacca Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul11.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Unlike the Pāli placement in the *Mahāvagga*, the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* assigns the *Satya-saṁyukta* to the *Nidānavagga* [Bodhi 2000]. Individual discourses, such as the *Papātasutta* (SN 56.42) and *Mahāpariḷāhasutta* (SN 56.43), warn of the dire consequences of ignorance of the truths and find parallels in the Gāndhārī Senior scroll collection (Senior 8) and Sanskrit fragments [Marino 2017]. An early North Indian inscription from the 2nd–3rd century CE also quotes the four noble truths, likely drawing from this collection [Winternitz 1933]. DharmaNexus confirms these cross-language alignments with SĀ (T 99) and aligns passages with texts such as the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, *Catuṣpariṣatsūtra*, and *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, alongside Tibetan parallels in the *Vinayavastu* and *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pāli canon, DharmaNexus detects over 20,000 matches shared across 351 texts, predominantly with the *Aṅguttaranikāya* (AN 4, AN 3, AN 1) and related *Saṁyutta* collections (SN 13, SN 22, SN 12) [DharmaNexus].
